records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔יד זֶ֣ה ה֔וּא בֵּ֖ית יְהוָ֣ה הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְזֶה־מִּזְבֵּ֥חַ לְעֹלָ֖ה לְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: And said David, This [is] [the] house of Yahweh the God, and this [is the] altar for burnt offering for Israel.
pieces: Then David declared, "Here is the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God, and here is the altar of burnt offering for Israel."

L.1: And David said, "This [is] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God, and this [is] the altar for burnt offering for Israel."

R.1: Then David said, "The house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God will be here, and this will be the altar where Israel offers burnt offerings."

decisions.choice: this is the house of the LORD God: this place is where God's house is to stand
alternatives: this is the house of the LORD God (the building already present)
decisions.reason: David speaks at the threshing floor of Ornan, where he had built an altar and the LORD answered him with fire from heaven (21:18-28). No building stands there yet; David declares the spot to be the site of the house and its altar. 2 Chronicles 3:1 says Solomon built the house there, on Mount Moriah. The verse closes the story of chapter 21 and opens the account of David's preparations.

decisions.choice: the LORD God: the divine name joined to "the God"
decisions.reason: The divine name is followed by "the God", a rare pairing that stresses that the LORD is the one true God. Verse 19 uses it again for the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: will be here; this will be the altar where Israel offers burnt offerings
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that David is naming the site of a house still to be built (m1), and spells out "altar of burnt offering for Israel" as the place where the people's offerings will be made.

records.heading: David prepares to build the temple

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔יד לִכְנוֹס֙ אֶת־הַגֵּרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּאֶ֣רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיַּעֲמֵ֣ד חֹֽצְבִ֗ים לַחְצוֹב֙ אַבְנֵ֣י גָזִ֔ית לִבְנ֖וֹת בֵּ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And said David to gather the sojourners who [were] in [the] land of Israel; and he appointed stonecutters to cut stones of hewn [stone] to build [the] house of the God.
pieces: So David gave orders to gather the outsiders who were living in the land of Israel, and he set stonecutters to cut dressed stones for building the house of God.

L.2: And David said to gather the sojourners who [were] in the land of Israel, and he appointed stonecutters to cut dressed stones to build the house of God.

R.2: So David ordered that the outsiders living in the land of Israel be brought together. These were people who were not Israelites. He put some of them to work as stonecutters, shaping blocks of stone to build God's house.

decisions.choice: said to gather: gave orders to gather
decisions.reason: The verb "say" followed by an infinitive is a king's command, as in 15:16 and 21:17.

decisions.choice: the sojourners: people of non-Israelite descent living in Israel
decisions.reason: A sojourner was someone living among Israel without being an Israelite by birth, with some protection under the law but no inherited land. Solomon later counted such people and set them to work as stonecutters and carriers (2 Chronicles 2:16-17; compare 1 Kings 9:20-22). The stonecutters David appoints here are most likely drawn from them.

decisions.choice: dressed stones: blocks cut and squared for building
decisions.reason: The noun names stone cut to shape with tools, as for the foundations of the temple (1 Kings 5:31) and the palace (1 Kings 7:9); Exodus 20:25 forbade such stone for an altar, but not for a house.

decisions.choice: These were people who were not Israelites. He put some of them to work as stonecutters
decisions.reason: Readable explains "outsiders" (m2) and shows that the workers came from them, which the context implies (2 Chronicles 2:16-17).

records.source: וּבַרְזֶ֣ל׀לָ֠רֹב לַֽמִּסְמְרִ֞ים לְדַלְת֧וֹת הַשְּׁעָרִ֛ים וְלַֽמְחַבְּר֖וֹת הֵכִ֣ין דָּוִ֑יד וּנְחֹ֥שֶׁת לָרֹ֖ב אֵ֥ין מִשְׁקָֽל׃
records.gloss: And iron in abundance for the nails for [the] doors of the gates and for the clamps prepared David, and bronze in abundance, there [was] no weight.
pieces: David provided a great deal of iron for nails for the doors of the gates and for clamps, and more bronze than could be weighed.

L.3: And iron in abundance for the nails for the doors of the gates and for the clamps David prepared, and bronze in abundance, without weight.

R.3: David got ready large amounts of iron to make nails for the gate doors and clamps to hold the building together. He also gathered so much bronze that no one could weigh it.

decisions.choice: prepared: laid up in advance, provided
decisions.reason: The verb means to make ready or set in place. It is the key word of the chapter (verses 3, 5 and 14): David cannot build the house, but he readies everything for it.

decisions.choice: clamps: fittings that join parts of a structure
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning "join". 2 Chronicles 34:11 uses it of timbers for joining a building; here they are of iron, so metal fastenings or couplings are meant.

decisions.choice: there was no weight: too much to weigh
decisions.reason: A way of saying the amount was beyond measuring, used of the bronze for Solomon's temple too (1 Kings 7:47).

decisions.choice: clamps to hold the building together
decisions.reason: Readable says what the clamps were for, in line with m2.

records.source: וַעֲצֵ֥י אֲרָזִ֖ים לְאֵ֣ין מִסְפָּ֑ר כִּֽי הֵ֠בִיאוּ הַצִּֽידֹנִ֨ים וְהַצֹּרִ֜ים עֲצֵ֧י אֲרָזִ֛ים לָרֹ֖ב לְדָוִֽיד׃פ
records.gloss: And wood of cedars without number, for brought the Sidonians and the Tyrians wood of cedars in abundance to David.
pieces: There were also cedar logs beyond counting, for the Sidonians and the Tyrians had brought great quantities of cedar to David.

L.4: And cedar logs without number, for the Sidonians and the Tyrians brought cedar logs in abundance to David.

R.4: There were also more cedar logs than anyone could count, because the people of the cities of Sidon and Tyre had brought David great amounts of cedar wood.

decisions.choice: Sidonians and Tyrians: the people of the Phoenician coastal cities who traded in cedar
decisions.reason: Sidon and Tyre lay on the coast north of Israel, near the cedar forests of Lebanon. Hiram king of Tyre had sent cedar for David's palace (14:1; 2 Samuel 5:11), and later supplied Solomon (1 Kings 5:20-24, where the Sidonians are named as skilled at cutting timber).

decisions.choice: for they had brought: the reason the cedar was so plentiful
decisions.reason: The clause explains the supply; the bringing came before David's preparations were complete.

decisions.choice: without number: more than could be counted
decisions.reason: Like "no weight" in verse 3, a way of stressing a vast amount.

decisions.choice: the people of the cities of Sidon and Tyre
decisions.reason: Readable names the cities so that young readers know who the Sidonians and Tyrians were.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗יד שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנִי֮ נַ֣עַר וָרָךְ֒ וְהַבַּ֜יִת לִבְנ֣וֹת לַיהוָ֗ה לְהַגְדִּ֨יל׀לְמַ֜עְלָה לְשֵׁ֤ם וּלְתִפְאֶ֨רֶת֙ לְכָל־הָ֣אֲרָצ֔וֹת אָכִ֥ינָה נָּ֖א ל֑וֹ וַיָּ֧כֶן דָּוִ֛יד לָרֹ֖ב לִפְנֵ֥י מוֹתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And said David, Solomon my son [is] young and tender, and the house to build for Yahweh [is] to make great upward, for a name and for splendor to all the lands; let me prepare, please, for it. And prepared David in abundance before his death.
pieces: David said, "Solomon my son is young and inexperienced, and the house that is to be built for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} must be made great beyond measure, so that its fame and splendor reach all lands. So let me get things ready for it." So before his death David laid up materials in great quantity.

L.5: And David said, "Solomon my son [is] young and tender, and the house to be built for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] to be made exceedingly great, for a name and for splendor to all the lands. Let me prepare for it." And David prepared in abundance before his death.

R.5: David said, "My son Solomon is young and has little experience. But the house built for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} must be very great. It must be famous and beautiful in every country. So I will get things ready for it." So David got a great amount of materials ready before he died.

decisions.choice: young and tender: young and inexperienced
decisions.reason: "Tender" (soft) describes someone not yet hardened by experience. David says the same of Solomon in 29:1. He is old enough to be made king (23:1), so the words do not mean a small child; compare Solomon's own humble words in 1 Kings 3:7.

decisions.choice: to make great upward: to make very great, to the highest degree
decisions.reason: "Upward" after "make great" is a way of saying "exceedingly". The house must be on a scale fit for the LORD.

decisions.choice: for a name and for splendor to all the lands: so that the house is renowned and admired in every land
decisions.reason: "Name" here means renown. The aim is that the house be known and honored among all nations, which brings honor to the LORD it is built for (compare 1 Kings 8:41-43).

decisions.choice: let me prepare for it: David's resolve
decisions.reason: The verb has the form of a wish or resolve, strengthened by the particle "please": since Solomon is young, David decides to do the preparing himself.

decisions.choice: laid up materials in great quantity / got a great amount of materials ready
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says David "prepared in abundance" without naming an object; verses 2-4 and 14 show it was building materials, and Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֖א לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנ֑וֹ וַיְצַוֵּ֨הוּ֙ לִבְנ֣וֹת בַּ֔יִת לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: And he called for Solomon his son and commanded him to build a house for Yahweh, God of Israel.
pieces: Then he summoned his son Solomon and charged him with building a house for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

L.6: And he called for Solomon his son and commanded him to build a house for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel.

R.6: Then David sent for his son Solomon. He gave him the task of building a temple for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: commanded him: gave him a solemn charge
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a father's or leader's last instructions, as David charges Solomon in 1 Kings 2:1 and Moses charges Joshua in Deuteronomy 31:23. Verses 7-16 give the words of the charge.

decisions.choice: a house for the LORD: a temple
decisions.reason: "House" is the usual word for a temple, the place where God's presence dwells among his people.

decisions.choice: David; temple
decisions.reason: Readable names David as the subject and says "temple" for "house", as Readable does through the chapter.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר דָּוִ֖יד לִשְׁלֹמֹ֑ה בְּנִ֕י אֲנִי֙ הָיָ֣ה עִם־לְבָבִ֔י לִבְנ֣וֹת בַּ֔יִת לְשֵׁ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽי׃
records.gloss: And said David to Solomon, My son, I, it was with my heart to build a house for [the] name of Yahweh my God.
pieces: David said to Solomon, "My son, it was my own desire to build a house for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God.

L.7: And David said to Solomon, "My son, as for me, it was in my heart to build a house for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God.

R.7: David said to Solomon, "My son, I wanted to build a temple to honor the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God.

decisions.choice: my son (the form read aloud)
alternatives: David said to Solomon his son
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text spell "his son", which would make the words part of the narration ("David said to Solomon his son"); the scribes' marginal note directs that it be read "my son", which makes it the opening of David's speech. The data follows the reading, and the sense hardly changes.

decisions.choice: it was with my heart: I intended, I wished
decisions.reason: To have something "with" or "in" one's heart is to plan or desire it, as David's wish to build is told in 17:1-2 and 28:2 (compare 1 Kings 8:17).

decisions.choice: a house for the name of the LORD: the place where the LORD makes himself known and is called on
decisions.reason: The "name" stands for the LORD himself as he reveals himself to his people. Deuteronomy 12:5 and 11 speak of the place he will choose "to put his name there", and Solomon's prayer returns to it (1 Kings 8:29).

decisions.choice: I: placed first for emphasis
decisions.reason: The pronoun stands at the front: "I, for my part". David sets his own wish against what the LORD said, which follows in verse 8.

decisions.choice: a temple to honor the name
decisions.reason: Readable explains "a house for the name" in line with m3, as 2 Samuel 7:13 does at Readable.

records.heading: David's charge to Solomon

records.source: וַיְהִ֨י עָלַ֤י דְּבַר־יְהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר דָּ֤ם לָרֹב֙ שָׁפַ֔כְתָּ וּמִלְחָמ֥וֹת גְּדֹל֖וֹת עָשִׂ֑יתָ לֹֽא־תִבְנֶ֥ה בַ֨יִת֙ לִשְׁמִ֔י כִּ֚י דָּמִ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים שָׁפַ֥כְתָּ אַ֖רְצָה לְפָנָֽי׃
records.gloss: And came to me [the] word of Yahweh, saying, Blood in abundance you have shed, and wars great you have made; not you will build a house for my name, for bloods much you have shed to the earth before me.
pieces: But the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me: 'You have poured out blood in great amounts and waged great wars. You will not build a house for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, because of all the blood you have poured out on the earth in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence.

L.8: But the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying, 'Blood in abundance you have shed, and great wars you have waged. You shall not build a house for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, for much blood you have shed on the earth before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.8: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message: 'You have killed many people and fought great wars. So you will not be the one to build a temple for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. You have spilled so much blood on the earth in front of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: David may not build the house because he has shed much blood in war
alternatives: the bloodshed counts as guilt against David
David was only prevented by being busy with war (1 Kings 5:17)
decisions.reason: Chronicles gives a reason the earlier books do not. In 2 Samuel 7:5-13 (1 Chronicles 17:4-12) the LORD simply says that he will build David a house and that David's son will build the house for his name. In 1 Kings 5:17 Solomon says David could not build because wars surrounded him on every side and kept him busy. Here (and in 28:3) the wars themselves make David unfit to build the house. His wars were fought with the LORD's help (18:6, 13), so this is not a verdict that they were wicked; rather, the house of rest is to be built by a man of rest and peace (verse 9), not by a warrior whose hands are marked by killing.

decisions.choice: shed blood: take human life, here in battle
decisions.reason: "Pour out blood" means to kill. The plural "bloods" in the second clause stresses many deaths.

decisions.choice: on the earth before me: on the ground, in the LORD's sight
decisions.reason: The blood soaks into the ground (compare Genesis 4:10-11; Deuteronomy 12:16), and the LORD has seen all of it.

decisions.choice: saying: introduces the LORD's own words
decisions.reason: David now quotes the word he received. The quotation runs to the end of verse 10; verse 11 is David speaking again. This word is not found in 1 Chronicles 17 or 2 Samuel 7.

decisions.choice: killed many people
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom "shed blood" (m2) the first time, then keeps "spilled blood" so the picture of verse 8b remains.

records.source: הִנֵּה־בֵ֞ן נוֹלָ֣ד לָ֗ךְ ה֤וּא יִהְיֶה֙ אִ֣ישׁ מְנוּחָ֔ה וַהֲנִח֥וֹתִי ל֛וֹ מִכָּל־אוֹיְבָ֖יו מִסָּבִ֑יב כִּ֤י שְׁלֹמֹה֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה שְׁמ֔וֹ וְשָׁל֥וֹם וָשֶׁ֛קֶט אֶתֵּ֥ן עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּיָמָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Here, a son [will be] born to you; he will be a man of rest, and I will give rest to him from all his enemies from round about; for Solomon will be his name, and peace and quietness I will give on Israel in his days.
pieces: Look, a son is to be born to you, and he will be a man of rest. I will grant him rest from all the enemies around him. For his name will be Solomon, and in his days I will give Israel peace and quiet.

L.9: Look, a son [is to be] born to you. He will be a man of rest, and I will give him rest from all his enemies all around; for Solomon will be his name, and peace and quiet I will give to Israel in his days.

R.9: Look, a son will be born to you. He will be a man of rest. I will let him live at rest, free from all the enemies around him. His name will be Solomon, a name that sounds like the word for peace, and while he lives I will give Israel peace and quiet.

decisions.choice: Solomon ... peace: a play on the name
decisions.reason: The name Solomon (Shelomo) sounds like the word for peace (shalom), and the LORD links them: "Solomon will be his name, and peace ... I will give." The name is read as a sign of what his reign will bring. 2 Samuel 12:24-25 says the LORD also gave him the name Jedidiah, "loved by the LORD".

decisions.choice: a man of rest; I will give him rest: freedom from war and enemies
decisions.reason: "Rest" (menuchah) here is safety from enemies, a settled peace in the land. The LORD had promised such rest as the time when the place for his name would be chosen (Deuteronomy 12:10-11), and Solomon later says that rest has come (1 Kings 5:18). The noun and the verb share a root: the man of rest is given rest. Verse 18 takes up the same verb.

decisions.choice: a son will be born to you: a promise about the future
alternatives: a son has been born to you
decisions.reason: The participle points ahead to a birth still to come, from the time the word was given.

decisions.choice: peace and quiet: security and calm in the land
decisions.reason: "Quiet" is the word used in Judges for the land at rest from war (Judges 3:11); together with "peace" it describes a reign free of war.

decisions.choice: a name that sounds like the word for peace
decisions.reason: Readable explains the wordplay (m1), which is lost in translation.

records.source: הֽוּא־יִבְנֶ֥ה בַ֨יִת֙ לִשְׁמִ֔י וְהוּא֙ יִהְיֶה־לִּ֣י לְבֵ֔ן וַאֲנִי־ל֖וֹ לְאָ֑ב וַהֲכִ֨ינוֹתִ֜י כִּסֵּ֧א מַלְכוּת֛וֹ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: He will build a house for my name, and he will be to me for a son, and I to him for a father; and I will establish [the] throne of his kingdom over Israel until forever.
pieces: He is the one who will build a house for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. He will be a son to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will be a father to him, and I will make the throne of his kingdom over Israel firm forever.'

L.10: He will build a house for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and he will be to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a son, and I [will be] to him a father, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.'

R.10: He is the one who will build a house to be a temple that honors {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. He will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} son, and I will be his father. And I will make sure that his throne as king over Israel will last forever.'

decisions.choice: the promise of 2 Samuel 7:13-14 (1 Chronicles 17:12-13), applied to Solomon by name
decisions.reason: These are the words of the LORD's promise to David through Nathan. There are differences: here "he will be my son" comes before "I will be his father" (the order is reversed from 2 Samuel 7:14 and 1 Chronicles 17:13); the throne clause comes last and adds "over Israel"; and the warning of 2 Samuel 7:14b about punishing the son when he does wrong is absent, as it is in 1 Chronicles 17:13. Nathan spoke of "your offspring"; David now names Solomon as the one meant.

decisions.choice: he will be my son, and I will be his father: a bond of covenant care and loyalty
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 7:14, the words describe the king's adoption into a close relationship with the LORD, who will care for him and to whom he owes loyalty (compare Psalm 2:7). Hebrews 1:5 quotes them of the Son.

decisions.choice: he will build: he, not you
decisions.reason: The pronoun is stated for emphasis, setting Solomon against David's "you shall not build" in verse 8.

decisions.choice: forever: for all time to come
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 7:13, the promise to establish the throne has no end in view.

decisions.choice: wording reused from 2 Samuel 7:13-14
decisions.reason: Where the Hebrew matches 2 Samuel 7:13-14, all three levels keep the wording used there ("establish", "make firm", "a house to be a temple that honors my name"), changing only what m1 lists.

records.source: עַתָּ֣ה בְנִ֔י יְהִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה עִמָּ֑ךְ וְהִצְלַחְתָּ֗ וּבָנִ֨יתָ֙ בֵּ֚ית יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר עָלֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Now, my son, may be Yahweh with you, and you will succeed and you will build [the] house of Yahweh your God, as he spoke concerning you.
pieces: Now, my son, may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be with you, so that you prosper as you build the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised concerning you.

L.11: Now, my son, may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be with you, and may you succeed and build the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has spoken concerning you.

R.11: Now, my son, may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be with you. May you do well and build the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised.

decisions.choice: may the LORD be with you, and you will succeed: a wish and its result
decisions.reason: The first verb is a wish; the next two carry it on, saying what will follow when the LORD is with Solomon. David now speaks again in his own words, after quoting the LORD in verses 8-10.

decisions.choice: succeed: carry the work through to a good end
decisions.reason: The verb means to prosper or to bring a task to completion. It returns in verse 13, where success depends on keeping the LORD's law.

decisions.choice: just as he promised concerning you
decisions.reason: "Spoke concerning you" refers to the word just quoted in verses 9-10, which is a promise; Balanced and Readable say "promised".

records.source: אַ֣ךְ יִֽתֶּן־לְּךָ֤ יְהוָה֙ שֵׂ֣כֶל וּבִינָ֔ה וִֽיצַוְּךָ֖ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלִשְׁמ֕וֹר אֶת־תּוֹרַ֖ת יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Only may give to you Yahweh insight and understanding, and he will put you in charge over Israel, and to keep [the] law of Yahweh your God.
pieces: Above all, may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} grant you insight and understanding when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sets you over Israel, so that you keep the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.12: Only may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} give you insight and understanding when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} puts you in charge over Israel, so as to keep the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.12: Most of all, may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} make you wise and give you understanding when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes you ruler over Israel. Then you will be able to obey the teaching of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: insight and understanding: good sense and the ability to judge rightly
decisions.reason: The two words describe practical wisdom for ruling. Solomon later asks the LORD for exactly this (1 Kings 3:9; 2 Chronicles 1:10).

decisions.choice: and he will put you in charge: when he sets you over Israel
alternatives: and may he put you in charge over Israel
decisions.reason: The clause is joined by "and" and may be read as the time when the insight is needed ("when he puts you in charge") or as a further wish ("and may he put you in charge"). Either way Solomon's rule is the LORD's appointment.

decisions.choice: and to keep the law: the purpose of the gift
decisions.reason: The infinitive says what the insight is for: so that Solomon keeps the LORD's law as king.

decisions.choice: the law of the LORD: the LORD's instruction given through Moses
decisions.reason: The word means teaching or instruction, the whole of what the LORD gave Moses for Israel, as verse 13 goes on to say.

decisions.choice: Above all / Most of all; teaching (Readable)
decisions.reason: The opening word ("only") singles this wish out as the one that matters most. Readable says "teaching" for the law, as 1 Kings 2:3 does at Readable.

records.source: אָ֣ז תַּצְלִ֔יחַ אִם־תִּשְׁמ֗וֹר לַעֲשׂוֹת֙ אֶת־הַֽחֻקִּ֣ים וְאֶת־הַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֖ה עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל חֲזַ֣ק וֶאֱמָ֔ץ אַל־תִּירָ֖א וְאַל־תֵּחָֽת׃
records.gloss: Then you will succeed, if you take care to do the statutes and the judgments which commanded Yahweh Moses for Israel. Be strong and be bold; do not fear and do not be dismayed.
pieces: Then you will succeed, if you are careful to carry out the statutes and the rulings that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded Moses for Israel. Be strong and courageous. Do not fear or lose heart.

L.13: Then you will succeed, if you take care to do the statutes and the judgments that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded Moses for Israel. Be strong and bold; do not fear and do not be dismayed.

R.13: You will do well if you are careful to obey the laws and rules that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Moses for Israel. Be strong and brave. Do not be afraid or lose hope.

decisions.choice: be strong and bold; do not fear or be dismayed: the charge to Joshua
decisions.reason: These are the words Moses and the LORD spoke to Joshua (Deuteronomy 31:6-8; Joshua 1:6-9), and the promise of success through keeping the law echoes Joshua 1:7-8. As Moses prepared and Joshua finished the conquest, David prepares and Solomon is to finish the house. David repeats the charge in 28:20; compare 1 Kings 2:2-3.

decisions.choice: then you will succeed, if: success depends on keeping the law
decisions.reason: The promise of verse 11 is tied to a condition: Solomon will succeed if he obeys.

decisions.choice: statutes and judgments: the LORD's laws and rulings
decisions.reason: The pair sums up the commands given through Moses: fixed laws and decisions for cases.

decisions.choice: be dismayed: be shattered, lose heart
decisions.reason: The verb describes being broken in spirit by fear, as in Joshua 1:9.

decisions.choice: be strong and bold (Literal); be strong and courageous (Balanced); be strong and brave (Readable)
decisions.reason: The charge keeps the wording used for Joshua (Joshua 1:9), so the echo can be heard (m1).

records.source: וְהִנֵּ֨ה בְעָנְיִ֜י הֲכִינ֣וֹתִי לְבֵית־יְהוָ֗ה זָהָ֞ב כִּכָּרִ֤ים מֵֽאָה־אֶ֨לֶף֙ וְכֶ֗סֶף אֶ֤לֶף אֲלָפִים֙ כִּכָּרִ֔ים וְלַנְּחֹ֤שֶׁת וְלַבַּרְזֶל֙ אֵ֣ין מִשְׁקָ֔ל כִּ֥י לָרֹ֖ב הָיָ֑ה וְעֵצִ֤ים וַאֲבָנִים֙ הֲכִינ֔וֹתִי וַעֲלֵיהֶ֖ם תּוֹסִֽיף׃
records.gloss: And here, in my affliction I have prepared for [the] house of Yahweh gold, talents a hundred thousand, and silver, a thousand thousands talents, and the bronze and the iron there [is] no weight, for in abundance it is; and wood and stones I have prepared, and to them you will add.
pieces: Look, with hard toil I have provided for the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} {{units:about 7,500,000 pounds|100,000 talents}} of gold and {{units:about 75,000,000 pounds|1,000,000 talents}} of silver, and bronze and iron beyond weighing, there is so much of it. I have also provided timber and stone, and you are to add to them.

L.14: And look, in my affliction I have prepared for the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gold, 100,000 talents, and silver, 1,000,000 talents, and bronze and iron without weight, for it is in abundance; and timber and stones I have prepared, and to them you will add.

R.14: I have worked hard to get things ready for the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I have stored up {{units:about 3,750 tons|100,000 talents}} of gold and {{units:about 37,500 tons|1,000,000 talents}} of silver. There is so much bronze and iron that it cannot be weighed. I have also gathered wood and stone, and you must add more.

decisions.choice: in my affliction: with great effort and hardship
decisions.reason: The noun means affliction, hardship or lowliness. It may mean David gathered these things through hard toil, or in the middle of the troubles of his reign, or in his humble state compared with the greatness of the task. The first fits David's point best: he has gone to great lengths for the house.

decisions.choice: 100,000 talents of gold and 1,000,000 talents of silver: an immense amount, perhaps not meant as an exact figure
alternatives: exact weights of the usual talent
decisions.reason: At about 75 pounds to the talent, this is about 3,750 tons of gold and 37,500 tons of silver, far beyond any other figure in Scripture: Solomon's yearly gold was 666 talents (1 Kings 10:14), and David's own later gift is 3,000 talents of gold and 7,000 of silver (29:4). The numbers may be deliberate overstatement, matching "beyond weighing" in the same verse, to stress that David spared nothing; they may be round sums; or the talent used may have been lighter than the usual one. The Hebrew gives no hint which, and the figures are translated as written.

decisions.choice: there is no weight, for it is in abundance: too much to weigh
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, the bronze and iron are said to be beyond measuring.

decisions.choice: to them you will add: an instruction to Solomon
decisions.reason: The future verb here gives Solomon his task: he is to add to what David has gathered.

decisions.choice: about 7,500,000 pounds; about 75,000,000 pounds (Balanced); about 3,750 tons; about 37,500 tons (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the weight in modern measure, with the talents as the alternative, as 1 Kings 10:14 does; Readable rounds to tons, which are easier to picture. Literal keeps the talents.

records.source: וְעִמְּךָ֤ לָרֹב֙ עֹשֵׂ֣י מְלָאכָ֔ה חֹצְבִ֕ים וְחָרָשֵׁ֥י אֶ֖בֶן וָעֵ֑ץ וְכָל־חָכָ֖ם בְּכָל־מְלָאכָֽה׃
records.gloss: And with you in abundance [are] doers of work: stonecutters and craftsmen of stone and wood, and every skilled [one] in every work.
pieces: You also have workers in great numbers: stonecutters, craftsmen in stone and wood, and every kind of worker skilled for every task.

L.15: And with you in abundance [are] doers of work: stonecutters and craftsmen of stone and wood, and every skilled [one] in every work.

R.15: You have plenty of workers too. There are people who cut stone, builders who work with stone and wood, and people skilled in every kind of work.

decisions.choice: stonecutters; craftsmen of stone and wood: those who quarry stone, and those who shape and build with stone and timber
decisions.reason: The first word names the men who cut stone from the rock (as in verse 2); the second names skilled builders and carpenters who work the stone and wood into the house.

decisions.choice: skilled: wise in a craft
decisions.reason: The word usually translated "wise" also means skilled in a trade, as of the craftsmen who made the tabernacle (Exodus 31:6; 35:10).

decisions.choice: workers; people skilled
decisions.reason: "Doers of work" and "every skilled one" do not name men or women; Balanced and Readable use words that are just as open.

records.source: לַזָּהָ֥ב לַכֶּ֛סֶף וְלַנְּחֹ֥שֶׁת וְלַבַּרְזֶ֖ל אֵ֣ין מִסְפָּ֑ר ק֣וּם וַעֲשֵׂ֔ה וִיהִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה עִמָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Of the gold, of the silver, and of the bronze and of the iron there is no number. Arise and act, and may be Yahweh with you.
pieces: The gold and silver, the bronze and iron, are beyond counting. Now get up and go to work, and may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be with you."

L.16: Of the gold, of the silver, and of the bronze and of the iron there is no number. Arise and act, and may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be with you."

R.16: You have more gold, silver, bronze and iron than anyone can count. So get started on the work, and may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be with you!"

decisions.choice: of the gold ... there is no number: the metals are beyond counting
alternatives: skilled in gold, silver, bronze and iron, without number
decisions.reason: The verse can be read as its own sentence about the metals, or as carrying on verse 15: craftsmen skilled "in gold, silver, bronze and iron", beyond number. The words "there is no number" stand after the metals, which favors the first reading.

decisions.choice: arise and act: begin the work
decisions.reason: "Arise" before another command urges action, as the LORD says to Joshua "arise, cross" (Joshua 1:2); it does not mean standing up.

decisions.choice: may the LORD be with you: a blessing
decisions.reason: David closes his charge with the wish he began with in verse 11.

decisions.choice: get up and go to work / get started on the work
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps a hint of the "arise" picture; Readable gives the plain sense (m2).

records.source: וַיְצַ֤ו דָּוִיד֙ לְכָל־שָׂרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לַעְזֹ֖ר לִשְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בְנֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And commanded David all [the] princes of Israel to help Solomon his son.
pieces: Then David ordered all the officials of Israel to help his son Solomon.

L.17: And David commanded all the princes of Israel to help Solomon his son.

R.17: Then David told all the leaders of Israel to help his son Solomon.

decisions.choice: the princes of Israel: the leading men and officials of the nation
decisions.reason: The word names men with authority: tribal heads, royal officials and commanders. Chapter 23 begins the lists of the leaders and Levites David gathered.

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); officials (Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: The usual wording for this title in these books.

records.source: הֲלֹ֨א יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙ עִמָּכֶ֔ם וְהֵנִ֥יחַ לָכֶ֖ם מִסָּבִ֑יב כִּ֣י׀נָתַ֣ן בְּיָדִ֗י אֵ֚ת יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ וְנִכְבְּשָׁ֥ה הָאָ֛רֶץ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה וְלִפְנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: [Is] not Yahweh your God with you, and has he given rest to you from round about? For he has given into my hand the inhabitants of the land, and is subdued the land before Yahweh and before his people.
pieces: "Is not {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God with you? Has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not given you rest on every side? For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has handed the people who lived in the land over to me, and the land lies subdued before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

L.18: "[Is] not {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God with you? And has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not given you rest all around? For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given into my hand the inhabitants of the land, and the land is subdued before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

R.18: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is with you. He has given you rest from war on every side. He has let me defeat the people who lived in the land, and now the land is under the control of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

decisions.choice: is not the LORD with you, and has he not given you rest?: questions that expect "yes"
decisions.reason: The questions state what the leaders already know. David speaks to them directly, though the Hebrew does not introduce the speech with "saying".

decisions.choice: rest all around and the land subdued: the time for the LORD's house has come
decisions.reason: Rest from enemies was the sign that the place for the LORD's name should be built (Deuteronomy 12:10-11; 2 Samuel 7:1). "The land was subdued before them" recalls Joshua 18:1, when the tent of meeting was set up at Shiloh once the land was won. The word "rest" also ties back to the "man of rest" of verse 9.

decisions.choice: given into my hand: given me victory over
decisions.reason: To give someone "into the hand" of another is to put them in his power.

decisions.choice: statements in place of questions; rest from war; let me defeat
decisions.reason: Readable turns the questions into the statements they imply (m1), says what the rest was from, and explains "given into my hand" (m3).

records.source: עַתָּ֗ה תְּנ֤וּ לְבַבְכֶם֙ וְנַפְשְׁכֶ֔ם לִדְר֖וֹשׁ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם וְק֗וּמוּ וּבְנוּ֙ אֶת־מִקְדַּשׁ֙ יְהוָ֣ה הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים לְהָבִ֞יא אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֗ה וּכְלֵי֙ קֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים לַבַּ֖יִת הַנִּבְנֶ֥ה לְשֵׁם־יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: Now set your heart and your soul to seek Yahweh your God; and arise and build [the] sanctuary of Yahweh the God, to bring [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh and [the] vessels of holiness of the God into the house [to be] built for [the] name of Yahweh.
pieces: Now set your heart and soul on seeking {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Get up and build the sanctuary of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God, so that the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the sacred vessels of God can be brought into the house that is to be built for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

L.19: Now set your heart and your soul to seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and arise and build the sanctuary of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God, to bring the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the holy vessels of God into the house built for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

R.19: Now commit yourselves with all your heart and soul to seeking {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Start building the holy place of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God. Then the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the holy objects used in God's worship can be carried into the temple built to honor the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: set your heart and your soul: give your whole self
decisions.reason: "Heart" is the mind and will, and "soul" (nefesh) the whole living self with its desires. Together they mean complete devotion, as in Deuteronomy 4:29 and 6:5.

decisions.choice: seek the LORD: turn to him in worship and obedience
decisions.reason: To seek the LORD is to look to him, worship him and ask his will. It is a key theme of Chronicles: Saul died because he did not seek the LORD (10:13-14), and the ark was neglected in his days (13:3).

decisions.choice: the ark and the holy vessels: brought together into one house
decisions.reason: The ark was in a tent in Jerusalem (16:1; 17:1), while the tabernacle and its altar stood at Gibeon (16:39; 21:29). The new house will bring them together; 2 Chronicles 5:2-7 tells how it was done.

decisions.choice: sanctuary; the house to be built: the holy place still to be built
decisions.reason: "Sanctuary" means a holy place set apart for God. The participle "built" points to a house not yet standing.

decisions.choice: holy place; holy objects used in God's worship
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for "sanctuary" and "holy vessels" and keeps "ark", as these books do.
